What to post and what NOT to post on /v/fantasywriters.

As mentioned in the sidebar text, there are things we encourage you to post and things we don’t. The moderation team of /v/fantasywriters reserves the right to change these policies at any time. If they change, there will be a notification.

ALLOWED:

  • Discussions, questions and critiques related or relevant to your FANTASY WRITING.

(Yes, YOUR fantasy writing and FANTASY writing. This also means you have to indicate this in your POST. Sadly none of the mods are psychic (yet) so if it is not immediately obvious your post is related or relevant to your fantasy writing, we may remove it.)

  • Self-promotion, within reason. Got published? Good for you! However, to avoid spam, absolutely all self-promotion posts must be for works that are either scheduled for publication or have been published within the past 12 months.

NOT ALLOWED:

  • General writing questions and discussion. This means questions about tenses, point of view, grammar, punctuation, UNLESS you relate it specifically to a piece of YOUR writing. General writing discussion should be directed to /v/writing.

  • General questions related to publishing and marketing. Unless you relate it to your writing.

  • General discussions about fantasy writers or fantasy works that are not your own.

  • Direct links to blogs. Please host your work somewhere else.

REALLY NOT ALLOWED:

  • General history questions and discussions.

(Yes, even ones on MEDIEVAL HISTORY! No matter how badly you need to know how medieval people made soap, it is not allowed. Why? Because we are not Wikipedia, and history is not always relevant to fantasy, which covers a wide range of topics.)

How Reddit the Business Lost Touch With Reddit the Culture

I agree with and enjoyed most of the article... I feel like they got a lot of things right that others have gotten horribly wrong... right up until the end. When it said that they had more than a little confidence reddit would get back on track, though, I laughed out loud. Clearly they don't realize that a lot of redditors are on to the game, and every tiny little continued effort to monetize and commercialize the site is going to destroy it a little bit more.

Reddit is going to be an interesting case study for businesses of the future. They have the critical mass to be successful, but the site has totally turned its back on it's core values and users. That usually doesn't work out in the real world (or Digg).

Reddit is going to be an interesting case study for businesses of the future

I definitely agree on this. I don't mean to post Reddit-related articles to contribute to the Reddit-sucks circle jerk, but it's just incredibly fascinating to see how it all unfolds. What interests me the most is that Reddit, a for-profit company, depends on volunteer users to ensure continuity of its business. It makes me wonder if the outcome would have been better if Reddit was non-profit and have the knowledge/skill set to approach its volunteer mods with a volunteer management perspective.

Additionally, much of the literature I've read re: technology and the importance of change management relates to an employer-employee relationship. In this case, this is a company-end user relationship. Reddit may have benefitted from utilizing a change management approach with its users, but with the current events, it seems that Reddit just views users as a commodity rather than a resource.

*EDIT: typo

History repeats again. Management of a dotcom that's grown significantly becomes disconnected with their product and doesn't eat their own dog food. They manage by status reports and analytics, forgetting that the users are both the customer and the product and need to be deeply understood, respected and cultivated. The user base becomes numbers, as leadership loses grasp that these are business leaders, attorneys, medical professionals, artists, technicians, developers and so on - highly intelligent people and in many cases more capable than the dotcom management itself--and they do not take kindly to being treated like teenagers.

Source: I worked in community starting in 1983 for CompuServe when we were inventing the online forum and moderator (we called them sysops) tools, and later for AOL, Netscape.com and some other web brands.

I'm not really sure where to start and to be honest, it's hard to type much in my current condition. I've never asked for help in my life, even when I used to be homeless I refused to ask for assistance and instead tried to work myself out of every hole life threw me into. But that strong person feels like he is no longer, I feel broken and hopeless.

I started dating the person I'm currently seeing right as she was getting out of an abusive long term marriage. He left her with thousands of dollars in debt and took one of her dogs, a dog that she felt was like her own child. A few months of time passed and we eventually got word from his parents that he was in no mental condition to take care of the animal let alone himself, so we drove out to meet them and pick our baby girl back up. But something was wrong, she was not the same pup and now we fear he was abusing her.

Since returning home she has been involved in several fights with the other boy pup who assumed the role of lead dog since she left. One fight as so bad she had pierced his cheek with her teeth and as we were trying to pull them apart we saw it tearing and had to use something to pry them apart, all of which resulted in hundreds of dollars in vet trips.

On top of all of this we have had her oldest cat break her hip and have to make several trips to the vet herself after developing an infection in the broken area. The first trip to the vet they said they saw nothing wrong and discharged our cat, but we knew something was up. Then a day later we wake up to the dogs fighting. They had bitten into each other and got their fang stuck in the other's cheek. Blood was spraying everywhere and I had to reach in and dislodge the tooth. Strangely, this is not how I lost my finger. So we ended up having to take in the dogs for stitches and thought we might as well bring the cat in again too. That's when they gave us the bad news that the first vet missed something and our cat was going to need about $2000 worth of surgery. My girlfriend had pretty much broken down at this point and didn't know what to do so I sucked up my pride and made a crowdfundraiser for our cat. This only made things worse because she got more depressed when none of her friends chipped in but the brunt of the money came from people I knew. But all of that seems like nothing now as I look down at my bandaged hands typing these words out on a keyboard. Forcing myself past the sting of blinding pain that is typing at all and push these words past the fog in my head that is the pain medication starting to take affect.

After a failed night of trying to cheer ourselves up me and the girlfriend headed home for some quiet. She had been called into work on her last day of vacation and we just wanted it to be over. I sat there on her bed with two pups as the third boy walked upstairs. He had grown very close to me recently and became jealous when the others were near me. He saw them and began to growl, I reached out and calmed him down but the other pup started barking. I turned to push her aside to make room for him to come cuddle and that's when he lunged at her in full attack mode and I felt a sharp stabbing pain. I knew I was bit but had no idea how bad. I just clenched it and tried to separate them. My girl ran in when she heard the screaming and we worked to get them apart. I ran into the bathroom and wrapped my hand in a towel to stop the bleeding but didn't stop to look at the damage until she asked "is it gone" and as I peeled the towel back I saw something you should never see. Something you should never feel. A sight I can't stop seeing every time I close my eyes. I can't even describe how hard it is to write this post and be forced to relive this... but I saw it gone. The tip bursting with blood around the edges from where once my right hand ring finger was.

Shock set in and that is where things got blurry. I remember medics, being asked name age, etc and the several really painful nerve blocks that followed. If one has never felt a nerve block, the most I can say is imagine a root canal... in your finger... now imagine that process without painkillers times a thousand and that is what each needle feels like before the injection of burning fluids that force you to feel like your entire body is being torn apart on an atomic level. I had to receive several of these and yet this was not the worst pain I felt that night. Losing my finger, the injections, the shock, none of it was as bad as watching the woman I love more than my own life sit there by my side in tears, blaming herself for everything and coming to terms with the realization that she was going to have to put down one of her babies, the same one who despite all this is still my favorite. I can't even sleep anymore without seeing the images of her in tears replay over and over.

The next few days have been a blur of anxiety and torment. We're both broke and hopeless as medical bills start piling up for both of us and now and I might still lose more of my finger if it manages to get an infection. I'm out of work and quickly burning through sick time. Thankfully I do have good friends and coworkers who are helping us as much as they can, but it's still seeming hopeless despite it all. I'd like to think there's no way this can get worse, and I'm afraid to even try to make it better... because life just feels over right now. I can't even bring myself to talk to friends about this online, though I've tried. I know I've already tapped all of them out on cash for the cat so now it feels like I'm just shit out of luck. I guess it was just bad timing, either that or the ultimate case of no good deed goes unpunished.

If you'd like to see the NSFL/proof pics of the damage done you can find them here: http://imgur.com/a/BAPwS

And hey, I guess while we're at it, if you have any questions on what it feels like to lose a part of your finger through traumatic amputation, ask away. I'm not really doing anything else now.
